egypt.title: Flag of the Arab Republic of Egypt

colors.note: The red band symbolizes the Egyptians' blood in the war against colonization.
The white band symbolizes the purity of the Egyptian's heart.
The black band below the white, symbolizes the manner in which darkness is overcome.
The Eagle of Saladin (national emblem) centred on the white stripe.

desc: - A horizontal tricolour of red, white, and black with the gold Eagle of Saladin (national emblem) centred on
- the white stripe. The current design was adopted on 4 October 1984, deriving from the Arab Liberation Flag tradition
trivia:
- The Eagle of Saladin (Qurʾān eagle) is the same eagle used by several other Arab nations
- The red-white-black tricolour was designed during the 1952 Egyptian Revolution
- The colours represent the bloodshed of revolution (red), purity (white), and resistance (black)

egypt-uar.title: United Arab Republic Flag

colors.note: The two stars represented Egypt and Syria.

desc:
- The **United Arab Republic** (UAR; Arabic: الجمهورية العربية المتحدة‎ al-Jumhūrīyah al-'Arabīyah al-Muttaḥidah)
- was a sovereign state in the Middle East from 1958 to 1971. It was initially a political **union** between
- **Egypt** and **Syria** from 1958 until Syria seceded from the union after the 1961 Syrian coup d'état
- Egypt continued to be known officially as the United Arab Republic until 1971
- **Construction:** three equal horizontal bands of red (top), white (middle), and black (bottom), with two green five-pointed stars centred on the white band
trivia:
- The United Arab Republic (1958–1961) briefly united Egypt and Syria
- The flag represented Pan-Arab unity and Nasserism
- Egypt continued using these colours after the union dissolved

egypt-revolution.title: Egyptian Revolution Flag
desc:
- The **Egyptian Revolution Flag** was used by the **Republic of Egypt** following the
- Egyptian Revolution of 1952
- **Construction:** the Liberation Flag — three equal horizontal bands of red, white, and black. Adopted during the Egyptian Revolution of 1952
trivia:
- The Revolutionary Egypt flag (1952–1958) represented the Nasser era
- Symbolised the end of monarchy and British influence
- Briefly used Pan-Arab colours during Egyptian-Syrian union

egypt-kingdom.title: Kingdom of Egypt
desc:
- The flag of the Kingdom of Egypt was green with a white crescent and three white stars
- It was used from 1922 until the revolution of 1952
- **Construction:** a green field with a white crescent and three white five-pointed stars centred
trivia:
- The Kingdom of Egypt (1922–1952) gained nominal independence from Britain
- The monarchy ruled during this period until the Egyptian Revolution
- The flag represented a transitional period in Egyptian sovereignty

desc: - The Sultanate of Egypt flag, a green and white design used 1914-1922
- **Construction:** a green field with a white crescent and three stars, similar to the Khedivate flag but under different sovereignty
trivia: - The Sultanate of Egypt (1914–1922) was declared by the British to formally sever Egypt's last ties with the Ottoman Empire during WWI
- Sultan Hussein Kamel was installed by the British to replace the Ottoman-aligned Khedive Abbas II

desc: - The Khedivate of Egypt flag with red field and white crescents and stars
- **Construction:** a red field with three white crescents, each with a white star, arranged vertically in the centre

colors.note: The traditional colour of Ottoman Egypt.

trivia: - The Khedive of Egypt held a title higher than Pasha but lower than Sultan — a unique Ottoman distinction
- Under Khedive Ismail, Egypt hosted the opening of the Suez Canal in 1869

territoryData.name: Egypt Eyalet
note: The Eyalet of Egypt operated as an administrative division of the Ottoman Empire from 1517 to 1867.
It originated as a result of the conquest of Mamluk Egypt by the Ottomans in 1517, following the
Ottoman–Mamluk War (1516–1517) and the absorption of Syria into the Empire in 1516.
The Ottomans administered Egypt as an eyalet of the their Empire (Ottoman Turkish: ایالت مصر‎‎ Eyālet-i Mıṣr)
from 1517 until 1867, with an interruption during the French occupation of 1798 to 1801.

desc:
- The flag of Ottoman Egypt (the Egypt Eyalet) was a red field, reflecting the suzerainty of the Ottoman Empire, which used red as its imperial colour
- Egypt was an Ottoman province from 1517 until the rise of Muhammad Ali Pasha, who established a semi-independent dynasty in the early 19th century
- **Construction:** a plain red field. Various crescent and star devices were sometimes added. Ratio approximately 2:3
trivia: - Ottoman Egypt was technically a province but operated with significant autonomy under Muhammad Ali's dynasty
- The red flag was shared with much of the Ottoman Empire, which used red as its imperial colour

desc: - The Mamluk Sultanate flag, a yellow standard used before Ottoman conquest
- **Construction:** a yellow field, sometimes bearing calligraphic or heraldic devices. Mamluk banners varied by sultan
trivia: - The Mamluk Sultanate was ruled by a military caste of originally enslaved soldiers — one of history's most unusual governance systems
- The Mamluks defeated both the Mongols (at Ain Jalut, 1260) and the Crusaders

eagle-of-saladin.title: Eagle of Saladin
desc: - A reconstruction of Saladin's personal standard, featuring the eagle
- **Construction:** a heraldic emblem — the Eagle of Saladin rendered in gold on a shield, used as a charge on several Arab national flags
trivia:
- The Eagle of Saladin is used on the flags of Egypt, Syria, Iraq, and Palestine
- Represents Arab nationalism and Islamic heritage
- Saladin is a legendary figure in Islamic history
